Key Research Thinking Patterns: Hybrid Model Synergy: Combining different AI techniques so one model's strengths compensate for another's weaknesses. (e.g., Using WGANs to generate synthetic data that enriches the dataset for a predictive XGBoost model or merging CNNs (for spatial analysis) with LSTMs (for temporal analysis)).

Data-Centric Problem Solving: Actively overcoming core data limitations, such as scarcity or privacy, as a primary step before model application. (e.g., Using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) or Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) for data augmentation to combat data scarcity, and employing Federated Learning to preserve patient data privacy).

Simulation-to-Reality Validation: Bridging computational theory and experimental reality by training models on simulated data and validating them against experimentally verifiable outcomes. (e.g., Training models on FDTD-simulated photonic data to discover novel, experimentally realizable geometries with high Q-factors, or training on computational (DFT) data to predict real-world synthesizable crystals confirmed in the ICSD).

Context-Aware Validation: Employing validation strategies that reflect real-world deployment challenges, such as temporal shifts and asymmetric error costs. (e.g., Training materials models on historical data (2011-2018) to test their predictive power on future, unseen data (2019-2025), and using adaptive thresholds to prioritize high recall, reflecting the greater cost of missing a synthesizable material).
Summary Description: Dr. Yaser 'Mike' Banad specializes in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, exploring their profound interplay with Materials Science, Smart Grid Energy Systems, Medical Diagnostics, and Photonics. His research focuses on developing robust hybrid frameworks, often leveraging Generative AI (WGANs, VAEs), Transformers (including LLMs), and Deep Learning (CNNs, U-Net). He applies these techniques to complex, data-centric challenges such as synthesizability prediction in crystalline materials, inverse design of photonic circuits, early diagnosis of Alzheimer's and brain tumors, and optimizing smart grid operations. Significant contributions include pioneering Positive-Unlabeled (PU) learning for materials discovery, applying Federated Learning for grid privacy, and integrating Digital Twins with AI, often validating computational models against real-world experimental data.
